anomalies.observed: On both 3-pin servo headers, pin 1 is tied to the servo power rail from D3 and the 100u capacitor bank, while pin 2 is tied to GND; pin 3 is the signal pin.
anomalies.expected: The servo power rail should connect to pin 2 of the servo headers, with pin 1 as GND and pin 3 as signal, per the specification.

evidence.quote: J9 pin 1 connects to the D3/capacitor servo rail; J9 pin 2 connects to GND; J11 pin 1 connects to the D3/capacitor servo rail; J11 pin 2 connects to GND (sheet 1).
D2 ... feeds a dedicated servo power rail backed by four 100 µF capacitors (C1–C4) before reaching J3/J8 pin 2.

anomalies.impact: A standard servo wired for GND on pin 1 and +5V on pin 2 would receive reverse polarity when plugged into these headers, likely preventing operation and potentially damaging the servo.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears to swap the servo power and ground pins on the 3-pin servo headers: the servo rail is on pin 1 and GND on pin 2, whereas the specification requires the servo power rail on pin 2.

In a typical auto-direction circuit for RS485, DE and /RE tied together, and a transistor inverts TX to DE. When UART TX idle high (3.3V), transceiver driver should be disabled (DE low) so it can receive. When TX starts (low for start bit), driver should enable (DE high). In a typical auto-direction circuit for RS485, DE and /RE tied together, and a transistor inverts TX to DE.
